text: In software development, Git branching helps teams work on new features without disrupting the main codebase. A developer creates a separate *feature branch* to safely write and test code for a specific task. Once the feature is complete, the team uses a *pull request* to propose changes. This allows others to review the code before it's added to the main project. After approval, the branch is merged, integrating the new work through a process called *merging*. This *version control workflow* keeps the project organized, prevents conflicts, and makes collaboration smoother for everyone involved.
